page.title: QuestKeeper case study · Samantha Paras
page.meta: How I built QuestKeeper, a D&D companion my group uses during games: what bothered me, what broke, what changed, and the receipts.
header.summary: A full-stack D&D 5e companion: rules reference, character sheets, leveling and live tables for the DM and players, in one place.
header.role: Role: Solo: design, build and deploy
header.status: Status: ● Live, in development · used by my D&D group
header.loadNote: First load can take about 20 seconds while the server wakes up.
part1.label: Part 1 · The story
bothered.p1: Finding rules during a game was a struggle. There was a fan wiki we used that had everything we needed, but it was hard to navigate and slow to find anything in the middle of a session. Mostly, Google was the middleman: search, open a tab, then another, then figure out which one actually answered the question.
bothered.p2: As a new player, it was a lot to take in, and the rules lived in one place while my character sheet lived somewhere else.
bothered.p3: That's the whole reason I started QuestKeeper.
who.p: Me, and the friends I play with. QuestKeeper was built around our table, and we use it during our games. That's the whole user base. No inflated numbers here.
first.h2: What I first thought the solution was
first.p1: A faster reference. The first version was a school final project: a search page and browsable lists of races, classes, spells and backgrounds, with the browser calling the public D&D 5e SRD API directly.
first.p2: It didn't have character sheets, accounts or anything for running a game. Those came later.
built.v01.label: v0.1 · Jul 2026 · It technically worked
built.v01.text: The school project: search plus reference pages, calling the SRD API straight from the browser, hosted on GitHub Pages.
built.v02.label: v0.2 · Aug 2026 · Same face, new skeleton
built.v02.text: The overall interface stayed the same. Underneath, I moved the SRD calls behind my own Express backend, merged the frontend and backend repos into one monorepo with both histories intact, and deployed to Render.
note.v02.text: One repo, because a single feature kept needing coordinated changes across two repos and two histories.
built.v05.label: v0.5 · Sep 2026 · Getting somewhere
built.v05.text: Character creation, a full character sheet and leveling, saved in the browser's local storage. The sheet was one long page.
built.v10.label: v1.0 · Oct 2026 · Now we're talking
built.v10.text: A full redesign, a tabbed sheet, accounts and saved characters in Supabase, guided beginner-friendly character creation, and live tables where the DM runs combat for the group.
note.v10.text: Two layout problems showed up in screenshots I took for this portfolio: an empty search panel and an overlapping ability-score row on phones. A little embarrassing. I fixed both the same day.
wrong.search.title: Search made you take an extra step.
wrong.search.text: The first search sent you to a results page with an empty "Select an item" panel, and nothing useful showed until you clicked. The routing improved in August. The empty panel only fully went away in October, after I saw it again in a portfolio screenshot.
wrong.acolyte.title: Only one background showed up, and I thought I'd broken it.
wrong.acolyte.text: Character creation offered exactly one background: Acolyte. I was sure it was a filtering bug. I traced the data path, and QuestKeeper wasn't dropping anything: the 2014 SRD only includes Acolyte. That turned a "bug fix" into a content and licensing decision. The Backgrounds page now also shows the 2024 SRD backgrounds, labeled by edition. Guided character creation still uses the 2014 list; how to bring 2024 backgrounds into creation is an open decision on the roadmap.
note.acolyte.text: Thought it was my bug. It was the source data.
wrong.sheet.title: The character sheet became one endless page.
wrong.sheet.text: Every feature added another section: attacks, spells, resources, equipment, feats, backstory, companion, notes. At level 1 the sheet was 3,073 pixels tall, and a Fighter still scrolled past spellcasting.
changed.paths.title: Two data paths
changed.paths.problem: Problem: Public rules data and private player data need different things.
changed.paths.decision: Decision: Rules requests go through my Express backend to the SRD API. Accounts, characters and tables go straight to Supabase.
changed.paths.why: Why: The backend gives the public data one place to add validation, caching and source information later. Private data is protected where it's stored: row-level security gives each player access to their own characters. The table-sharing policy grants the DM read access; it does not grant editing access.
changed.paths.link: How this works → Behind the Build
changed.tabs.title: A combat header and tabs instead of one long sheet
changed.tabs.problem: Problem: The single sheet was 3,073px at level 1, and sections that didn't apply still had to be scrolled past.
changed.tabs.decision: Decision: A persistent combat header, six tabs, and a Skills sidebar visible from any tab.
changed.tabs.why: Why: The combat numbers stay in view while you move between shorter, focused sections, instead of scrolling one 3,073px page mid-fight. A tab that doesn't apply, like Spells for a non-caster, isn't shown at all, which was simpler than show/hide toggles for every section. On desktop the Skills sidebar stays visible from any tab; on phones the tabs wrap into a grid and a Stats/Skills toggle takes the sidebar's place.
changed.homebrew.title: Homebrew-friendly editing
changed.homebrew.problem: Problem: Guided creation works from SRD data, but real characters pick up things the SRD doesn't have: homebrew items, DM-granted resources, feats from other books.
changed.homebrew.decision: Decision: Every core stat is directly editable, and every list accepts freeform entries.
changed.homebrew.why: Why: Characters that are actually being played change over time, so every stat needs to stay editable as the character changes, not just at creation. One shared editable-list component keeps add, edit and delete consistent across every section.

part2.label: Part 2 · The receipts
arch.title: Architecture
arch.1: React → Express → D&D 5e SRD API (2014 and 2024) → a consistent response wrapper
arch.2: React → Supabase: Auth, Postgres, Realtime, Storage
stack.title: Stack
stack.1: React 19, React Router and Vite on the frontend, with plain CSS and design tokens
stack.2: Node and Express as a thin layer in front of the SRD API
stack.3: Supabase for auth, Postgres with row-level security, Realtime for live tables, and Storage for portraits
tests.title: Tests and CI
tests.1: Vitest for game logic and React Testing Library for sheet components.
tests.2: GitHub Actions runs lint, tests and a build on every push and pull request (since Sep 2026).
tests.3: No backend or end-to-end tests yet.
secrets.title: Keeping DM secrets secret
secrets.1: Enemy HP and AC live in a table only the table's DM can read.
secrets.2: Attack rolls are checked by a database function that returns the result, not the AC.
secrets.3: The project README records local checks of the database functions using DM, player and outsider identities. Those checks are not currently included as automated tests in the repository.
a11y.title: Accessibility
a11y.3: Phone sheet layout fixed the same day it was spotted, with before and after screenshots
licensing.title: Content and licensing
licensing.text: QuestKeeper uses only SRD content released for reuse. A page being public doesn't mean it can be copied. That's why the fan wiki isn't used as a data source.
